Title: For Which It Stands…
Description: Commemorating the 250th Anniversary of the U.S., this major loan exhibition explores key moments in our country’s history through artworks depicting the American flag. Artworks on view challenge viewers to consider who the American flag truly represents and whether justice is available to all.

Title: Inside Out: Contexts for American Art
Description: Investigates the power of contextualizing selected artworks from the Museum’s collection, turning them “inside out” for viewers to engage with paintings, sculpture, prints, textiles, and photographs in creative ways.

Title: Rediscovering the Cos Cob Art Colony: A Tribute to Susan G. Larkin
Description: Features artwork that led Dr. Larkin to become the foremost expert on American Impressionism in Connecticut, along with etchings, watercolors, and books from art colony authors from her personal collection.

Title: The Holley Boarding House: Inspiring American Impressionism
Description: Celebrates the legacy of the Holley boarding house, which attracted artists and writers to its charming 18th-century home, inspiring the creativity that led to the founding of the first Impressionist art colony in Connecticut.

Title: Albrecht Dürer: Master Prints
Description: Features over forty woodblock prints and engravings showcasing the remarkable achievements of the German Renaissance master printmaker Albrecht Dürer. An extraordinary innovator, Dürer revolutionized printmaking in the late fifteenth and early sixteenth century.

Title: Structure, Light, Land
Description: Features Barbara Kasten’s work from multiple series, including Architectural Sites, Collisions, and Progressions, as well as new iterations of digital projections, cyanotypes, and sculptures. Kasten’s work infiltrates the grounds of The Glass House and responds to the site’s varied built environment and landscape.

Title: Peter Waite: Social Memory, Paintings 1987–2025
Description: An exhibition of paintings by Peter Waite, known for his large-scale architectural scenes that explore spaces where history, memory, and perception meet. Waite’s compositions capture the beauty and poignancy of overlooked corners and traces of life that remain when people are gone.

Title: Historic Presence
Description: Curated by Terri Moore, this exhibition features Brooklyn-based artist Taha Clayton’s portraits inspired by the 1930s to 50s, honoring the resilience, joy, culture, and dignity of elders. The exhibition includes works in oil, charcoal, and graphite, enhanced with props from the artist’s creative process.

Title: Echoes and Collisions: The Art of Frantz Patrick Henry in Conversation with Selections from the Edith A. Graham Collection of Haitian Art
Description: Artistic legacies and contemporary visions meet, creating a dialogue that oscillates between harmony and dissonance, connection and collision. This exhibition is free and open to the public.
